pages.titre: How to reach us about a figure.
pages.lede: The right first message names a figure with its source: each number on this site carries a declared source, so a dispute can start precisely. And it attaches no file: this tool exists so your documents stay with you, and that starts here.

sections.h2: Two ways to reach us, email and a public issue
html: Write to contact@cascade-routing.com: the direct channel. For anything worth deciding in the open (a disputed figure, a wrong line, a question others will have), open an issue at github.com/ArslaneSempai-ui/cascade-routing. An issue is public, so keep confidential material out of it: no client names, no records, no internal figures. Either way, attach no file: a channel for records is opened in the engagement letter, before signature, like every other term.

The page you are on and the figure you dispute: each one here has a declared source, so we can meet at it. If you disagree with a measurement, better than an argument: the record is sealed and the command is public, so bring your own rerun. If you measured your own cases, bring the report the tool wrote beside your CSV: it contains rates and intervals, and no values from your documents.

We receive none of your records, not even a sample. The tool exists so your documents never leave your machine; a sample attached to a public issue is published, and a clone, once made, cannot be recalled. If your question needs your data, the answer is a command that runs where the data lives, and we will point you to it.

Two shortcuts. On a fresh clone, node src/premiere-reponse.mjs prints the conclusion in under a second, with what would flip it. And the eight objections a bank's reviewers actually raise are already answered, mechanism by mechanism, in Appendix C, Questions below.

pages.titre: Not in the record. Nothing lives at this address.
pages.lede: This page was never measured, never sealed, never published: the address is wrong, or the page has moved. Everything that exists is one link away: the findings on the main screen, and the six appendices in the footer below.

Who publishes this, under which licences, served from where, and what this site does to its visitors, which is nothing. The one page of a sales site that is usually mumbled; here it follows the same rule as the rest: plain, sourced, short.

Static files, from GitHub Pages, out of the public repository. No server code of ours runs to show you this page.

sections.h2: What this site does to visitors: nothing
html: No cookies, no analytics, no tracking, no forms. The scripts on this site do two things only: the main screen synchronises its animation clock and tab title, and the appendix pages open their sections when you print. Switch them off and everything still works. Each figure displayed carries a declared source; the full declaration file is public, beside this page: releve.json, and the seal in the masthead is the content content hash of the sealed public record the figures come from.

The tool publishes its own errors: a retraction file lists each published conclusion that turned out to be wrong, held open by a test. This site inherits the rule: a corrected figure is corrected in the open, with the change recorded.
